name: Kakrahwa–Varanasi Highway
history: NH 28 runs entirely inside Uttar Pradesh, from the India–Nepal border post at Kakrahwa down to the holy city of Varanasi on the Ganga. The border end lies close to Lumbini and Kapilvastu, places linked to the life of the Buddha, so the road is an important route for pilgrims. Before the 2010 renumbering most of this corridor was known as NH 233; the name NH 28 earlier belonged to the Lucknow–Barauni highway.
facts: About 305 km long, entirely within Uttar Pradesh.
Links the Nepal border near Lumbini, the Buddha's birthplace, with Varanasi.
Passes close to Piprahwa in Siddharthnagar district, a famous Buddhist stupa site identified by many with ancient Kapilavastu.
Crosses the Ghaghara river near Tanda on its way south.
